clearedSpotChecks.check: Is the value frame hook that earlier clearances read the same code on every public revision: check_blocklist_and_create_log, before_frame_init, checked_frame_init, init_deferred_frame_with_transfer_log and init_precompile_frame_with_transfer_log in crates/evm/src/evm.rs on main, master, release/0.8, tag v0.8.6, commit b1179556 and tag v0.8.5.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched crates/evm/src/evm.rs from raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node at v0.8.6, v0.8.5, release/0.8, b11795567992a7bf51e7f538ae37e7f19d076e13 and main. The first four have the same sha256 (1ce0d1e6...), and main differs as a file. The text from check_blocklist_and_create_log to the EvmTr impl is identical on main and v0.8.6 by diff. On v0.8.6, line 534 refuses a value frame from or to address(0), lines 542-567 refuse a blocklisted sender or recipient, lines 571-593 refuse a recipient self-destructed in the transaction, lines 595-604 emit the EIP-7708 log only when from differs from to, and line 622 skips every check for a zero amount. raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for Cargo.toml at 37812c61 and at 8e8edb7a, so the source of the two builds that the public endpoints run is still unpublished. This item covers the published revisions only, and the item says so. None of these branches changes the amount moved. Each one turns the call into a failure, and src/types/Currency.sol:44-52 then reverts take through CustomRevert, so the delta change at src/PoolManager.sol:294 is undone with it.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3 of L-944: native take from the real PoolManager by eth_call with state overrides on both Arc endpoints and Ethereum, recipients including address(0), a blocklisted address, precompiles, Arc system addresses, the PoolManager itself and a self-destructing contract.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran my own read-only checks. arc_getVersion returns v0.8.6-rc1 (37812c61) on rpc.mainnet.arc.io and v0.8.6 (8e8edb7a) on arc.drpc.org, both at block 0x1f9d0fb. The PoolManager code is 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefix 6eb21c69298b064e, which matches networks.json. eth_call from the PoolManager with value 1 to address(0) reverts with Error('Zero address not allowed') on both endpoints. The same call to a codeless address succeeds. With a state override that sets slot keccak(account, 2) of 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000001 to 1, value 1 to that account fails with 'Blocked address' on both, and value 0 to it succeeds. That matches line 622 of evm.rs v0.8.6. These failures are the freeze hazards already filed as F-125 and F-049. They need the recipient to be the zero address or a blocklisted account, and placing an account on the blocklist is an issuer action. take moves nothing when the transfer fails, because the call at src/types/Currency.sol:47 failing reverts the whole take, the _accountDelta at src/PoolManager.sol:294 included. _settle at src/PoolManager.sol:349-364 credits msg.value only when the synced currency is native and reverts NonzeroNativeValue otherwise. I did not rerun the 17 driver scripts or the self-destruct case. The item says that the destroyed-in-transaction branch was not reached, and it records that as a low lead.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 of L-944: the last 2,000 mined Arc transactions in which the PoolManager sends or receives native USDC were rerun in the cycle 17 reference interpreter with Arc's value rules, and their logs, PoolManager slots and native balances were compared.
clearedSpotChecks.note: summary.json gives 2000 selected, 1769 equal on pass one and 126 equal on pass two, with no error entries. The residual entries I read have pmLogsEqual and pmNativeLogsEqual set to true and differ only in addresses of EntryPoints and the relayer 0x69460570. I pulled three selected transactions from rpc.mainnet.arc.io (0x9a99ac2b..., 0x28dcfb34..., 0x92ac934f...). Each has status 1 and a Transfer log from 0xff...fe with the PoolManager as sender or recipient, so the selection rule holds on those three. I did not rerun the interpreter. The check is limited in two ways. It models the value hook from the v0.8.6 source, so it tests whether the running builds agree with that model on the paths users take, and it cannot cover branches that no mined transaction reached. No Arc endpoint serves debug or trace methods, so frame outputs were compared only through the logs, storage and balances they leave. Within those limits, I found nothing that contradicts the clearance.
